transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-25 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~42 min | Recording: on
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (AuroraGrid Partnerships), Aisha Khan (AuroraGrid CTO), Ben Cho (AuroraGrid Infra)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. Um, quick round — could folks introduce themselves real quick?
[00:08] Carlos Mendez: Yeah hi, Carlos here, head of partnerships at AuroraGrid. We're a cloud provider focused on hybrid GPU capacity for enterprise ML.
[00:13] Aisha Khan: Aisha, CTO. Responsible for platform and infra.
[00:16] Ben Cho: Ben, infrastructure lead. I manage GPU clusters and network.
[00:20] Priya Desai: Hi all, Priya SE — I own partner integrations and benchmarks for Redwood. Nice to meet you.

[00:30] Jordan Lee: Cool thanks. High-level we wanted to understand AuroraGrid's partner goals — are you looking for an integration to resell Redwood's hosted API, or more of a managed/dedicated offering for mutual customers, or something else?
[00:40] Carlos Mendez: We're exploring three things: 1) reseller/integration into our marketplace, 2) co-managed dedicated pools where customers can purchase through AuroraGrid but we run underlying infra, and 3) offering Redwood Private as an on-prem or VPC option for regulated customers. So kinda all three.
[00:55] Jordan Lee: Great. That aligns with the typical partnership modes we support — we have our hosted API, Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU pools (SLA-backed), and Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem installs.

[01:10] Aisha Khan: A few technical constraints we have: most customers require VPC peering or private connectivity, KMS integration, and SOC2-level audit logs. Also some need strict data residency. How do you handle those?
[01:23] Priya Desai: For Private we ship a customer-controlled control plane and support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging. We also do network options like VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and on-prem air-gapped installs. For Dedicated we can co-locate pools in AuroraGrid regions if we do a joint procurement.
[01:40] Ben Cho: When you say Dedicated, is that full physical isolation or multi-tenant with tenant isolation?
[01:44] Priya Desai: Dedicated is tenant-isolated GPU pools — physical tenancy at the pool level. We can work with encryption-at-rest and key management. There are different sizing/cost tradeoffs.

[02:00] Carlos Mendez: Great. On the business side, what's the partner program look like? Revenue split or referral? Do you have an ISV/reseller agreement template?
[02:08] Jordan Lee: We have a partner program with options: referral (simple), reseller (rev share), and strategic integrations (joint go-to-market and co-sell). We typically start with a commercial scope and SOW; I can share the program deck and templates.
[02:20] Carlos Mendez: Perfect, yes please.

[02:30] Jordan Lee: Priya — can you talk through the technical onboarding and typical benchmark cadence?
[02:33] Priya Desai: Sure. For a new partner we usually do: architecture workshop, environment prep (networking, images, access), run a baseline benchmark — we measure latency P50/P95, throughput, and per-token cost. For GPU vendors we look at A100/H100 performance and quantization profiles. We also validate kernel compatibility and memory footprints.
[02:55] Aisha Khan: Do you require a specific image or runtime? We run a mix of Ubuntu 22 and custom images.
[03:00] Priya Desai: We provide container images and helm charts; for Private we do a customer-specific deployment. There can be some image tweaking but it's usually straightforward. Also note sometimes transcription: the runtime's called Redwood runtime, but customers see it as part of the package.

[03:20] Ben Cho: Latency SLOs — what do you guarantee for inference?
[03:23] Priya Desai: For Dedicated we have configurable SLOs depending on commit. Typical internal targets are P95 < 200ms for conversational models at short sequences; obviously model size and qps matter. For hosted API we publish performance profiles per-model.

[03:40] Carlos Mendez: We have enterprise customers that need guaranteed throughput — could we implement burst policies?
[03:44] Jordan Lee: Yes, Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscaling policies; we can set policies per-customer in the pool config and route requests by policy.

[03:55] Aisha Khan: Security questions — you mentioned audit logs. Do you integrate with our SIEM? And what about SOC2/ISO?
[04:02] Priya Desai: We can ship logs to your SIEM using secure forwarders, and we support SSO/SAML for RBAC. Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified and we have ISO docs; I'll attach the security packet.
[04:14] Carlos Mendez: Awesome, please send those.

[04:25] Jordan Lee: On the integration flow — if AuroraGrid wants to surface Redwood in the marketplace, are you thinking deep integration (billing passthrough) or simple referral link?
[04:33] Carlos Mendez: Ideally billing passthrough for a seamless customer experience. We'll need legal to look, obviously.
[04:38] Jordan Lee: We do support billing integrations and reseller contracts — requires a billing integration and agreement. We'll loop legal after we sign an MOU.

[04:50] Ben Cho: For co-located Dedicated pools, what's the expected ops involvement from AuroraGrid? Patch cycles, maintenance windows?
[04:58] Priya Desai: We handle the runtime patching and model ops if we're operating the pool (Redwood-managed). If it's customer-managed but in your data center, we provide automation and runbooks; maintenance windows are coordinated.

[05:15] Carlos Mendez: Let's talk about a concrete pilot. What would you need from us to run a benchmark for one of our enterprise customers?
[05:22] Priya Desai: For a pilot benchmark we'd ask for: target model(s) and sizes, sample prompts / corpus, expected qps, sequence length distribution, network topology (peering details), and if possible, a test account with API keys. Also GPU type and region details.
[05:35] Aisha Khan: We can provide the infra diagram and GPU inventory. We have mix: in us-west we have 40xA100, 24xH100 across two racks.
[05:44] Priya Desai: Perfect, that helps. We'll propose a baseline: 1k requests at varying qps to get latency and cost curves. We'll also test quantized variants to see cost savings.

[05:58] Jordan Lee: Carlos — from a GTM standpoint, are there co-marketing expectations like webinars, case studies?
[06:03] Carlos Mendez: Yes, we'd prefer at least co-branded PR and a joint solution brief. If the pilot shows strong results, we'll push it into marketplace and sales motions.

[06:15] Jordan Lee: Good — we can support with a partner PR kit and case study template.

[06:25] Ben Cho: A couple of nitty-gritty networking Qs: do you support AWS PrivateLink only, or generic VPC peering and cross-connects?
[06:33] Priya Desai: We support multiple options: AWS PrivateLink, VPC peering, VPN, and dedicated interconnects. For Private deployments we can also do no-internet air-gapped setups.

[06:48] Aisha Khan: On data retention — can we control logs/metrics retention for compliance? Some customers need logs deleted after 30 days.
[06:56] Priya Desai: Yes, retention policies are configurable and we can scope persistence. For Private you control retention fully. For hosted we have configurable retention tiers and enterprise controls.

[07:10] Carlos Mendez: Any known limitations with specific GPU vendors? For instance, we work with NVIDIA but also experiment with other accelerators.
[07:17] Priya Desai: The runtime is optimized for NVIDIA (A100/H100) and Ampere/Hopper architectures. We also support other accelerators where kernel compatibility exists, but performance profiles vary. We sometimes see minor kernel mismatch warnings that require tuning.
[07:30] Jordan Lee: Competitors like CoreWeave and Lambda are common, but our differentiator is the unified runtime + rollout tooling and quality monitoring — helps partners offer predictable economics.

[07:45] Carlos Mendez: Sounds good. From an integration standpoint, timeline expectations? If we sign a pilot MOU, how long to run the pilot and produce deliverables?
[07:53] Priya Desai: Typically 2-4 weeks for a benchmark pilot: 1 week for environment prep and access, 1 week for baseline runs, and 1 week for analysis + report. Could be shorter depending on artifacts provided.

[08:07] Aisha Khan: Legal/compliance: can you share your SOC2 and ISO docs? Also do you have a standard data processing addendum?
[08:14] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll attach the security packet and DPA. Legal will share reseller templates after intro.

[08:25] Ben Cho: For telemetry and tracing — do you expose per-route metrics so customers can attribute cost per-team?
[08:31] Priya Desai: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. You can tag requests for chargeback.

[08:44] Carlos Mendez: Are there SSO options for partners accessing consoles?
[08:47] Priya Desai: SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC controls — we can provision partner roles.

[08:55] Jordan Lee: Quick note on pricing — two levers: unit pricing (per-token / per-embedding) and committed capacity pricing for Dedicated. We'll share a sample grid in the deck.

[09:05] Aisha Khan: For the pilot, we'd prefer committed capacity pricing to ensure predictable latency.
[09:09] Jordan Lee: We can propose a small committed pool for pilot customers; pricing depends on commit term and GPU mix.

[09:20] (brief cross talk / laughter)

[09:25] Carlos Mendez: Ok next steps recap? Jordan to send deck and security docs, Priya to draft benchmark plan, and we'll share infra details.

[09:33] Jordan Lee: Correct — I'll send partner deck, SOW template, and security packet by Monday (2026-09-28). Priya will follow up with benchmark plan and artifact list. Carlos/Aisha will share infra diagram and GPU counts.

[09:44] Aisha Khan: We'll also loop in our partnerships legal — I'll intro them in the thread.

[09:50] Jordan Lee: Great. Anything else?

[09:52] Ben Cho: One more: do you have examples of prior cloud partners?

[09:56] Priya Desai: Yes, we've partnered with multiple providers — can share references (short list) in the deck.

[10:05] Carlos Mendez: Sounds good. Thanks everyone, we'll review and get the artifacts posted.

[10:10] Jordan Lee: Thanks all. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for a kickoff once docs are shared.

End of recording.

Notes/References: partner deck link (placeholder): https://redwood.ai/partners/deck (will send); security packet: /link/security-packet (attached in follow-up).
